A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RCB framework, theoretical guarantees, simulations, and warfarin application despite the changed title. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic experiments and a warfarin dosing evaluation, including results averaged over 10 patient-arrival permutations, in Section 5 and Appendix J.

after.justification: v2 retains original warfarin results in Section 5 and the synthetic experiments and additional dosing results in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The cold-start procedure, IPGS equations, and Algorithms 1–2 remain substantively unchanged. However, v2 Section 3.2 says the spread parameter uses all historical data, while its formula and Algorithm 2 still specify the preceding epoch. This inconsistency prevents determining whether that data-use procedure changed.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic scenarios and the PharmGKB application with 5,528 patients, 70 constructed features, and three dosage arms. Moving simulations into Appendix F and framing dosing as clinical decision support do not introduce new evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: The always-Medium physician comparison and literature-based Lasso Bandit benchmark are retained. v2 explicitly identifies the Lasso reference line in Figure 2; its new literature-comparison Table 1 does not add experimentally evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 replaces v1's evaluation-criteria description of regret as an optimal mean-dose gap with an incorrect-decision count and explicitly defines error rate as R(T)/T. Both already describe binary rewards, and the continuous ground-truth construction and plots remain unchanged, so this establishes a reported metric revision rather than a demonstrated rerun.

E4.justification: The environment sensitivity, ad-hoc cold-start sizes, incentive-budget/prior-variance tests, and prior-decay misspecification analyses are retained from v1 Section 5.1 and Appendix J in v2 Appendix F. New scalability suggestions and clinical interpretations add discussion, not tested analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions average the dosing results over 10 random patient-arrival permutations and retain the same plotted uncertainty displays. No new seed counts, confidence intervals, significance procedures, or implemented uncertainty estimators are reported; bootstrap and conformal methods are only suggested for nonlinear extensions.

E6.justification: The corresponding empirical curves and dosage-table entries are unchanged. v2 omits the weighted risk scores 0.289 and 0.274 reported in v1, retaining 0.291 and 0.265. It also corrects the prose assigning the physician's 100% accuracy to Low dosage: v2 correctly identifies Medium, consistent with both tables.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 and the appendix proofs remain substantively unchanged. v2 adds oracle-complexity statements and revises Theorem 2 to use tilde-O notation and Tcold approximately equal to m0. That duration definition conflicts with the retained proof's round count, tau_(m0-1) = 2^(m0-1), rather than merely renaming it.

C1.justification: v1 explicitly conditions its advertised BIC guarantee on Gaussian priors. v2's contribution statement claims independence from specific posterior forms, and its new conclusion extends the advertised modularity to nonlinear oracles, although Theorem 1 remains Gaussian. It also elevates the already-derived cold-start tradeoff into a central 'price of incentives' contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantial discussion of large-K limitations and four mitigation strategies, nonlinear-oracle qualifications, expert supervision, and transparency risks. It also strengthens clinical interpretations, treating the retained 2% extreme-error rate as evidence of preserved safety constraints and emphasizing benefits for high-risk patients without new supporting experiments.

D1.justification: v2 removes v1's guidance that MSPE is typically estimated through cross-validation and its statement that code is available; neither supplied PDF provides a code-access link. The detailed feature processing and experimental hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: v2 substantially repositions RCB against fixed-design linear bandits, black-box reductions, and posterior-sampling approaches, including a new comparison table. It adds works such as Kalvit et al. (2024) and Dai et al. (2024), while substantially condensing the earlier medical-trial, incentive, and information-design survey.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, algorithm explanations, theoretical discussion, and clinical interpretation are extensively rewritten. Algorithms move to Appendix B, simulations move to Appendix F, related work is condensed, and new conclusion and impact sections reshape the narrative.

P2.justification: v2 introduces a two-column main layout, a new RCB flowchart, and a literature-comparison table. Existing algorithms and simulation figures are relocated, several appendix plot grids become horizontal strips, and captions are revised. These are substantial display changes despite largely unchanged empirical content.

improvement.justification: The overview diagram, focused positioning, and practical discussion improve accessibility. However, v2 introduces a mismatch between Theorem 2's cold-start duration and its retained proof, and advertises broader prior/oracle and clinical-safety claims without corresponding theoretical or empirical support. These losses in technical precision outweigh the presentation gains, while the underlying experiments and proofs remain largely intact.
